description: Least-privilege permissions for the dashboard and overlay windows. The content-protected meeting and update notification panels are deliberately isolated in notifications.json: their event subscriptions need only core:event:default, while their other calls invoke this application's own commands, which the ACL does not gate. Keeping their capability narrower than this core:default boundary closes KNEG-168, where both were absent from every capability and therefore could render nothing during a live recording. Both identifiers must be named in tauri.conf.json's security.capabilities allow-list, or the file is inert -- KNEG-171 was notifications.json missing from it. Notably absent: any http, shell, fs, or process permission. The frontend has no network access and cannot spawn anything -- it asks Rust, and Rust decides. Global shortcuts and autostart are driven from Rust, so the frontend needs no permission for either. See docs/NETWORK_BOUNDARY.md and docs/SECURITY.md.
